questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Drill 1: Consecutive equal time interval difference rule

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 1: Consecutive equal time interval difference rule

hints: For two consecutive equal intervals of duration $T$, the difference in distance travelled is $\Delta s = aT^2$.
Substitute values: $52 - 40 = a(2^2) \implies 12 = 4a \implies a = 3\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

walkthrough.text:
Set up equations for the distances in the two consecutive 2-second intervals:
$$s_1 = u(2) + \frac{1}{2}a(2^2) = 2u + 2a = 40$$
$$s_1 + s_2 = u(4) + \frac{1}{2}a(4^2) = 4u + 8a = 40 + 52 = 92$$

Subtract twice the first equation from the second, or apply the interval difference formula directly:
$$\Delta s = s_2 - s_1 = aT^2$$
$$52 - 40 = a(2^2) \implies 12 = 4a \implies a = 3\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Recall the consecutive interval theorem:
- When time windows are identical ($T = 2\text{ s}$), extra distance is produced by acceleration:
$$\Delta s = a T^2$$

Compute acceleration:
- Evaluating the gap between segments:
$$52 - 40 = a(4) \implies 4a = 12 \implies a = 3\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
The car accelerates at $3\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Applies $\Delta s = aT^2$ with $T = 2$, or sets up simultaneous equations $2u + 2a = 40$ and $2u + 6a = 52$.
Solves to obtain acceleration $a = 3\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Drill 2: Speed at the boundary between two equal time intervals

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 2: Speed at the boundary between two equal time intervals

hints: Under constant acceleration, the instantaneous speed at the time midpoint of an interval equals the average speed over the entire interval.
The total time is $2 + 2 = 4\text{ s}$ and total distance is $40 + 52 = 92\text{ m}$. Thus $v(2) = \frac{92}{4} = 23\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the average speed across the entire 4-second journey:
$$v_{\text{avg}} = \frac{\text{Total distance}}{\text{Total time}} = \frac{40 + 52}{2 + 2} = \frac{92}{4} = 23\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Relate average speed to the midpoint instantaneous speed:
$$\text{Because acceleration is uniform, } v(t_{\text{mid}}) = v_{\text{avg}}$$
$$v(2) = 23\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Use the midpoint velocity property:
- For constant acceleration, the velocity at the temporal midpoint equals the mean speed:
$$v(2) = \frac{s_{\text{total}}}{t_{\text{total}}}$$

Evaluate mean speed:
- Summing distance and time:
$$v(2) = \frac{40 + 52}{4} = \frac{92}{4} = 23\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
The speed at the boundary is $23\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Calculates overall average speed $\frac{40 + 52}{4}$ or uses $s_1 = vt - \frac{1}{2}at^2$ with $a = 3$.
Obtains speed at boundary $v = 23\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Drill 3: Distance travelled during the n-th second of motion

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 3: Distance travelled during the n-th second of motion

hints: The distance in the 5th second is the displacement from $t = 4\text{ s}$ to $t = 5\text{ s}$: $s_5 = s(5) - s(4)$.
Calculate $s(5) = \frac{1}{2}(4)(25) = 50\text{ m}$ and $s(4) = \frac{1}{2}(4)(16) = 32\text{ m}$. Difference is $50 - 32 = 18\text{ m}$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the total displacement at $t = 4\text{ s}$ and $t = 5\text{ s}$ using $s = \frac{1}{2}at^2$:
$$s(5) = \frac{1}{2}(4)(5^2) = 2(25) = 50\text{ m}$$
$$s(4) = \frac{1}{2}(4)(4^2) = 2(16) = 32\text{ m}$$

Subtract $s(4)$ from $s(5)$ to find the distance travelled during the 5th second:
$$s_5 = s(5) - s(4) = 50 - 32 = 18\text{ m}$$
Alternatively, apply $s_n = u + \frac{1}{2}a(2n - 1) = 0 + 2(9) = 18\text{ m}$.

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Apply the single-second interval method:
- Distance during the 5th second equals displacement gain from $t = 4\text{ s}$ to $t = 5\text{ s}$:
$$s_5 = s(5) - s(4)$$

Compute the difference:
- Evaluating displacements:
$$s_5 = \frac{1}{2}(4)(25 - 16) = 2 \times 9 = 18\text{ m}$$
The particle travels $18\text{ m}$ during the 5th second.

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Drill 4: Speed at the spatial midpoint between two fixed points

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 4: Speed at the spatial midpoint between two fixed points

hints: At the spatial midpoint $M$, distance $AM = MB = \frac{s}{2}$.
Use $v^2 = u^2 + 2a(s/2)$ for each half to deduce $v_M = \sqrt{\frac{u^2 + v^2}{2}} = \sqrt{\frac{7^2 + 17^2}{2}} = \sqrt{\frac{338}{2}} = \sqrt{169} = 13\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

walkthrough.text:
Apply $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ to each half of the journey where distance $d = AM = MB$:
$$v_M^2 - 7^2 = 2ad$$
$$17^2 - v_M^2 = 2ad$$

Equate the two expressions to solve for $v_M$:
$$v_M^2 - 49 = 289 - v_M^2$$
$$2v_M^2 = 338 \implies v_M^2 = 169 \implies v_M = 13\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Set up midpoint relation in space:
- Equal displacements produce equal changes in squared velocity:
$$v_M^2 - u^2 = v^2 - v_M^2 \implies v_M^2 = \frac{u^2 + v^2}{2}$$

Evaluate midpoint velocity:
- Substituting values:
$$v_M = \sqrt{\frac{49 + 289}{2}} = \sqrt{169} = 13\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
The speed at the spatial midpoint is $13\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Applies $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ over half-distances to establish $v_M^2 = \frac{u^2 + v^2}{2}$.

$$16a = 24 \implies a = 1.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

hints: Distance travelled during the $n$-th second is $s_n = s(n) - s(n-1) = u + \frac{1}{2}a(2n - 1)$.
For the 3rd second ($n = 3$): $u + \frac{1}{2}a(5) = 34 \implies u + 2.5a = 34$.
For the 6th second ($n = 6$): $u + \frac{1}{2}a(11) = 46 \implies u + 5.5a = 46$.
Subtract equations: $3a = 12 \implies a = 4\text{ m s}^{-2}$. Then $u = 34 - 2.5(4) = 24\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

walkthrough.text:
Express the displacement during the 3rd second ($t = 2$ to $t = 3$) and 6th second ($t = 5$ to $t = 6$):
$$s_3 = \left[3u + \frac{1}{2}a(9)\right] - \left[2u + \frac{1}{2}a(4)\right] = u + 2.5a = 34$$
$$s_6 = \left[6u + \frac{1}{2}a(36)\right] - \left[5u + \frac{1}{2}a(25)\right] = u + 5.5a = 46$$

Subtract the first equation from the second to find acceleration $a$:
$$(u + 5.5a) - (u + 2.5a) = 46 - 34$$
$$3a = 12 \implies a = 4\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Substitute $a = 4\text{ m s}^{-2}$ back to determine initial speed $u$:
$$u + 2.5(4) = 34 \implies u + 10 = 34 \implies u = 24\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Formulate consecutive single-second expressions:
- General formula for distance in the $n$-th second:
$$s_n = u + \frac{1}{2}a(2n - 1)$$
- Applying to 3rd and 6th seconds:
$$u + 2.5a = 34$$
$$u + 5.5a = 46$$

Solve linear system:
- Eliminating $u$:
$$3a = 12 \implies a = 4\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
- Finding $u$:
$$u = 34 - 10 = 24\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
The initial speed is $24\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and acceleration is $4\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Solves simultaneous equations to obtain $a = 4\text{ m s}^{-2}$ and $u = 24\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
